bundles.rationale: The move asserts that pervasive suffering appears gratuitous and conflicts with an all-powerful, all-loving God. This supports the pro subsidiary-1 bridge: if the proposition is true, suffering is less probable under that God, so compatibility fails. The pro central bridge is excluded because the move does not yet weigh evil against the combined positive arguments or address broader epistemic confusion.

bundles.evidenceText: belief in the existence of God is more rational than the alternative
bundles.rationale: The move asserts that the three arguments cumulatively make God more probable and belief in God more rational than nonbelief. This supports the con motion bridge because it expressly states the complete motion-level conclusion and cannot remain true without making that conclusion more credible. The con central bridge is excluded because its additional claim that responses prevent suffering from defeating the inference is not expressed here.

bundles.evidenceText: it isn't it cannot be that God
bundles.rationale: The move grants the positive arguments arguendo but denies that they can identify the all-powerful, all-loving God because that identification conflicts with the observed world. This directly attacks the con central inference from the combined arguments to the proposed God, and the proposition cannot remain true without limiting that inference. The pro central bridge is excluded under nearest exclusion because this is framed as a direct rebuttal of the con cumulative inference, so contact stays with the bridge attacked.

bundles.evidenceText: it's a collection of different books
bundles.rationale: The move asserts that biblical books use different genres and that some narrated stories are parables rather than historical events. That proposition is compatible with every stated route bridge and neither supports nor attacks any necessary premise concerning evil, salvation conditions, reason, design, morality, or the motion conclusion. The nearest pro subsidiary-2 bridge is excluded because the move says nothing about disputed salvation requirements or grave eternal consequences.
